questions.question: Which type of spherical mirror has its reflecting surface curved outwards and possesses a centre of curvature C that lies behind the mirror?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Convex mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror** is a type of **spherical mirror** where the **reflecting surface** is curved **outwards**, away from the center of the sphere.
 
• In a **convex mirror**, the **centre of curvature (C)** and the **principal focus (F)** are situated **behind the mirror**. This is because the mirror is part of a sphere whose center lies on the non-reflecting side.
 
• Because the reflected rays appear to originate from a point behind the mirror, it is also known as a **diverging mirror**. Parallel rays of light falling on it diverge after **reflection**.
 
• The **focal length** of a **convex mirror** is always considered **positive** according to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**.
 
• Regardless of the position of the object, a **convex mirror** always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirror (Converging Mirror):**
 
 
• The **reflecting surface** is curved **inwards**, towards the center of the sphere.
 
• The **centre of curvature (C)** and **focus (F)** lie in **front** of the mirror.
 
• It can form both **real and virtual images** depending on the object's distance from the **pole**.
 
• **Applications**: Used in **torches**, **search-lights**, **shaving mirrors**, and by **dentists** to see large images of teeth.
 
 
 
• **Plane Mirror:**
 
 
• A **plane mirror** has a **flat** reflecting surface.
 
• The **radius of curvature** and **focal length** of a **plane mirror** are **infinite**.
 
• It forms a **virtual and erect** image that is the **same size** as the object and **laterally inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Common Uses of Convex Mirrors:**
 
 
• They are widely used as **rear-view mirrors** in **vehicles** because they provide a **wider field of view** and always produce an **erect image**.
 
• They are installed in **shops** and **ATMs** as **security mirrors** to monitor a large area.
 
• Used at **blind turns** on roads to help drivers see **oncoming traffic** from the other side.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** For a **convex mirror**, the **magnification** is always **less than 1** (m < 1) and is **positive**, indicating a **diminished and erect** image.
 
• **Relationship between R and f:** The **radius of curvature (R)** is twice the **focal length (f)**, expressed as **R = 2f**.
 
• **Reflection Laws:** Both **concave** and **convex mirrors** obey the **laws of reflection**: the **angle of incidence** is equal to the **angle of reflection**, and the **incident ray**, **reflected ray**, and **normal** all lie in the same plane.
</ul

questions.question: In the case of unbalanced forces acting on an object, the acceleration (a) produced is in the direction of the ______________.

options.text: net force (resultant force) acting on the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**net force (resultant force) acting on the object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**, the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the **net force** acting upon it and inversely proportional to its **mass**.
 
• The mathematical representation of this law is **F = ma**, where **F** represents the **resultant or net force**, **m** is the **mass**, and **a** is the **acceleration**.
 
• In the case of **unbalanced forces**, the sum of all individual forces acting on the body is **not zero**. This non-zero sum is what we define as the **net force**.
 
• Because **mass** is a **positive scalar** quantity, the direction of the **acceleration vector** must always be identical to the direction of the **net force vector**. ***Hence, the statement in the question is satisfied by the net force.***
 
• If multiple forces act on an object, it is not the **largest individual force** or the **force of friction** alone that determines the direction of acceleration, but the **vector sum** of all forces combined.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Balanced vs. Unbalanced Forces**:
 
 
• **Balanced Forces**: When the **net force** is **zero**, the object is in **equilibrium**. It will either remain at rest or continue moving at a **constant velocity**.
 
• **Unbalanced Forces**: When the **net force** is **greater than zero**, it always results in a change in the object's state of motion, meaning it **accelerates**.
 
 
 
• **Net Force (Resultant Force)**:
 
 
• It is the **vector sum** of all the forces acting on an object. For example, if a force of **10 N** acts to the right and **4 N** acts to the left, the **net force** is **6 N** to the right.
 
 
 
• **Newton (Unit)**:
 
 
• The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**. **One Newton** is defined as the force required to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at a rate of **1 m/s²**.
 
 
 
• **Inertia**:
 
 
• Relating to **Newton's First Law**, **inertia** is the inherent property of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or motion. The **mass** of an object is a quantitative measure of its inertia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Direction of Velocity vs. Acceleration**: It is important to note that acceleration does not necessarily align with the **initial velocity**. For instance, in **circular motion** or when a car brakes, the acceleration direction can be perpendicular or opposite to the direction of motion.
 
• **Friction**: The **force of friction** usually opposes the **relative motion** between surfaces. While it is a component of the net force, it does not solely dictate the direction of acceleration unless it is the only unbalanced force acting on the body.
 
• **Vector Nature**: Since **force** and **acceleration** are **vector quantities**, they have both **magnitude** and **direction**. The direction of the **resultant force** is found using the **parallelogram law** or **triangle law** of vector addition.
 
• **Mass Influence**: For a constant **net force**, if the **mass** of an object is doubled, the **acceleration** will be halved, highlighting the **inverse relationship** between mass and acceleration.

questions.question: An object moves 10 m in 2 s. On a distance–time graph, what is the slope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **slope** of a **distance-time graph** represents the **speed** of an object. In physics, the slope is defined as the vertical change (rise) divided by the horizontal change (run).
 
• For a distance-time graph, the **distance** is plotted on the **Y-axis** (vertical) and **time** is plotted on the **X-axis** (horizontal).
 
• In the given problem, the **total distance** moved by the object is **10 m** and the **time interval** is **2 s**.
 
• The formula to calculate the **slope** is: **Slope = Change in Distance / Change in Time**.
 
• By substituting the values, we get: **Slope = 10 m / 2 s = 5 m/s**. ***Hence, the calculated value is 5 m/s.***
 
• This result tells us that the object is traveling at a **constant speed** of **5 meters per second** if the graph is a straight line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Speed vs. Velocity:** 
 
 
• **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** that refers to "how fast an object is moving." It only has **magnitude** and is calculated as **distance divided by time**.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** that refers to "the rate at which an object changes its position." It requires both **magnitude** and **direction** and is calculated as **displacement divided by time**.
 
 
 
• **SI Units:** The **International System of Units (SI)** unit for speed is **meters per second (m/s)**. Other commonly used units include **kilometers per hour (km/h)** and **miles per hour (mph)**.
 
• **Types of Motion on a Graph:**
 
 
• A **straight line** with a positive slope indicates **uniform motion**, meaning the object moves at a **constant speed**.
 
• A **curved line** indicates **non-uniform motion** or **acceleration**, where the speed of the object is changing over time.
 
• A **horizontal line** (parallel to the time axis) indicates that the **slope is zero**, meaning the object is at **rest** (speed is **0 m/s**).
 
 
 
• **Steepness:** The **steeper** the slope of the line on a distance-time graph, the **higher** the speed of the object. A line closer to the time axis represents a slower speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Graphical Interpretation:** To find the **instantaneous speed** at any point on a non-linear distance-time graph, one must draw a **tangent** to the curve at that specific point and calculate its slope.
 
• **Negative Slope:** On a **displacement-time graph**, a **negative slope** indicates that the object is moving back toward the **starting position**. However, on a **distance-time graph**, the slope cannot be negative because total distance covered never decreases with time.
 
• **Comparison:** If two lines are drawn on the same graph, the one with the higher **gradient** represents the object with the greater speed. For example, a line with a slope of **10 m/s** is steeper than the one calculated in this question (**5 m/s**).
 
• **Conversion:** To convert speed from **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply the value by **3.6** (or **18/5**). Therefore, **5 m/s** is equivalent to **18 km/h**.
</ul

questions.question: The colour of silver chloride changes when placed in sunlight for some time due to the:

options.text: Photochemical decomposition of silver chloride by sunlight
Combination reaction of silver chloride with oxygen
Displacement reaction by oxygen and water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photochemical decomposition of silver chloride by sunlight**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silver chloride** (**AgCl**) is a **white** crystalline solid that is sensitive to light. When it is placed in **sunlight**, it undergoes a **photochemical decomposition** reaction.
 
• The **sunlight** provides the necessary **activation energy** to break the chemical bonds in the **silver chloride** molecule. This results in the formation of **silver metal** and **chlorine gas**.
 
• The **white** color of the salt changes to **grey** due to the accumulation of **metallic silver** particles. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• A **decomposition reaction** is a process where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. When this process is triggered by **photons** (light), it is specifically called **photolysis** or **photochemical decomposition**.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: **2AgCl (s) + Sunlight → 2Ag (s) + Cl2 (g)**. The **chlorine gas** evolved during the process typically escapes into the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Silver Bromide (AgBr):** Similar to silver chloride, **silver bromide** also undergoes **photochemical decomposition**. It changes from a **pale yellow** color to **grey** when exposed to light.
 
• **Applications in Photography:** These reactions of **silver halides** (silver chloride and silver bromide) were the fundamental basis for **black and white photography**. The light falling on the photographic film would decompose the silver salts to create an image.
 
• **Storage Requirements:** Because of their high sensitivity to light, **silver salts** are always stored in **dark-colored** or **amber-colored bottles**. This prevents **sunlight** from reaching the chemicals and causing premature decomposition.
 
• **Types of Decomposition Reactions:**
 
 
• **Thermal Decomposition:** Triggered by **heat energy** (e.g., heating **calcium carbonate** to get **calcium oxide**).
 
• **Electrolytic Decomposition:** Triggered by **electrical energy** (e.g., **electrolysis of water** to get hydrogen and oxygen).
 
• **Photolytic Decomposition:** Triggered by **light energy** (e.g., decomposition of **AgCl** or **H2O2**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect Options Analysis:**

 
 
• **Combination reaction:** This involves two substances joining to form one. Silver chloride is breaking down, not combining with oxygen. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Thermal decomposition:** While heat is a form of energy, the specific change in silver chloride color in the presence of **sunlight** is categorized under **photochemical** processes because it responds to the **visible/UV spectrum** of light rather than ambient heat. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Displacement reaction:** This occurs when a more reactive element displaces a less reactive one from its compound. **Oxygen and water** do not displace chlorine from silver chloride in this context. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Observation:** The **grey** color is the most distinct physical evidence of the **chemical change** occurring, indicating that **pure silver** has been liberated from the compound.

questions.question: If Girl A takes 20 s and Girl B takes 50 s to climb a rope, both performing 3200 J of work, their difference in performance is characterised by which physical concept?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the **rate of doing work** or the rate at which energy is transferred or transformed. In this scenario, while both girls perform the same amount of work, the time taken differs, which directly affects the power output.
 
• The formula for Power is **Power (P) = Work (W) / Time (t)**. This indicates that power is inversely proportional to time when the work done is constant.
 
• For **Girl A**, the work done is **3200 J** and the time taken is **20 s**. Her power output is calculated as 3200 / 20 = **160 Watts**.
 
• For **Girl B**, the work done is **3200 J** and the time taken is **50 s**. Her power output is calculated as 3200 / 50 = **64 Watts**.
 
• Since the **total work done (3200 J)** is identical for both, the difference in their performance—where Girl A completes the task faster than Girl B—is specifically characterized by their **Power**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Power.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SI Unit of Power:** The standard unit of power is the **Watt (W)**, which is equivalent to **one Joule per second (1 J/s)**. It is named after the Scottish inventor **James Watt**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity:** Power is a **scalar quantity** because it only has magnitude and no specific direction. It depends only on the magnitude of work and the time interval.
 
• **Work and Energy:** **Work** is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force. In this question, both girls consumed **3200 J** of energy to perform the task, but the "speed" of that energy consumption is what defines power.
 
• **Gravitational Force:** This is the force of attraction between two masses. While the girls are working against gravity to climb the rope, the **gravitational force** acting on them depends on their **mass** and the **acceleration due to gravity (9.8 m/s²)**, not the time taken.
 
• **Total Displacement:** This refers to the change in position. Since both are climbing the same rope to the same height, their **total displacement** is equal and does not explain the difference in performance over time.
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for power is **[M¹ L² T⁻³]**. This is derived from the dimensions of work [M¹ L² T⁻²] divided by time [T].
 
• **Commercial Unit:** While Watt is the SI unit, **Horsepower (hp)** is often used in the automotive and engineering industries. **1 hp** is approximately equal to **746 Watts**.

questions.question: What is the benefit of developing dwarf broiler parents in poultry?

options.text: To make them resistant to rain
To reduce feed consumption and improve meat yield

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To reduce feed consumption and improve meat yield**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary benefit of developing dwarf broiler parents in the **poultry industry** is to significantly **reduce feed consumption** while maintaining high **meat yield** in the offspring.
 
• Dwarfism in poultry is typically managed through a **sex-linked recessive gene** known as the **dw gene**. When this gene is incorporated into the female parent line, it results in birds that are **25% to 30% smaller** in body weight than normal broiler breeders.
 
• Because of their smaller physical stature, these dwarf hens require much less **maintenance energy**, leading to a **20% to 25% reduction** in the amount of feed needed to sustain them. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Developing birds for **flight ability** or **rain resistance** is not a priority in commercial meat production, as broilers are kept in controlled environments to maximize weight gain. ***Hence, statements 1 and 2 are incorrect.***
 
• While dwarf parents are smaller, they are specifically bred to be mated with **normal-sized males**. This ensures that the **commercial progeny** (the broilers) grow to a full, standard size with excellent **meat-to-bone ratios**.
 
• Dwarf birds often produce **slightly smaller eggs** initially compared to standard hens, so the goal is not to "lay larger eggs" but to improve the **efficiency of egg production** per unit of feed. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Genetic Mechanism**: The **dw gene** is located on the **Z chromosome**. It affects the bird's metabolism by reducing the **plasma levels of Insulin-like Growth Factor-I (IGF-I)**, which results in shorter **shank length** and smaller body size without affecting general health.
 
• **Economic Efficiency**: In poultry farming, **feed costs** account for approximately **60% to 70%** of total production expenses. By using dwarf maternal lines, breeders can lower the cost of producing **day-old chicks**.
 
• **Stocking Density**: Because dwarf broiler parents are smaller, farmers can maintain a **higher stocking density** in poultry houses. This means more birds can be reared in the same **square footage**, optimizing the use of **infrastructure and labor**.
 
• **Environmental Adaptability**: Dwarf poultry often exhibit better **heat tolerance**. This is particularly advantageous in **tropical countries** like **India**, where high temperatures can cause heat stress in larger, heavier birds.
 
• **Reproductive Performance**: Dwarf hens are known for having fewer **reproductive disorders** (such as double-yolk eggs or internal laying) compared to standard heavy-weight broiler breeders, leading to more **viable hatching eggs** over the bird's **lifespan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **FCR (Feed Conversion Ratio)**: The use of dwarf parents improves the overall **biological efficiency** of the breeding operation, making the **poultry supply chain** more sustainable.
 
• **Meat Quality**: The offspring of dwarf mothers and normal fathers do not carry the dwarf trait (if the father is homozygous normal), ensuring the **final broiler** reaches **market weight** of **2.0 to 2.5 kg** within **35 to 42 days**.
 
• **Global Usage**: Major international breeding companies use dwarf female lines to cater to markets where **feed prices** are high or **housing space** is limited.

questions.question: Blood is called a connective tissue because ____________.

options.text: it connects and transports material throughout the body
it is found only in muscles

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**it connects and transports material throughout the body**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Blood** is classified as a **fluid connective tissue** because it shares the same **embryological origin** (the **mesoderm**) as other connective tissues like **bone** and **cartilage**.
 
• It serves as a **vital link** between different organ systems, effectively **connecting** all parts of the body by circulating through the **cardiovascular system**.
 
• The primary function of blood is the **transportation** of **respiratory gases** (**Oxygen** and **Carbon Dioxide**), **nutrients** (like **glucose** and **amino acids**), **hormones**, and **waste products** (like **urea**) to and from various tissues. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• Unlike other connective tissues that have a solid or semi-solid matrix, blood possesses a **liquid matrix** called **plasma**, in which **living cells** are suspended.
 
• Statement 2 is incorrect because blood is found within **blood vessels** (**arteries**, **veins**, and **capillaries**) distributed throughout the **entire body**, not just in **muscles**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3 is incorrect because while **ligaments** and **tendons** support bones, blood does not provide **mechanical support** to the skeletal structure; rather, it provides **metabolic support**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 4 is a physical characteristic, but the **red color** (caused by **hemoglobin** in **RBCs**) is not the biological reason for its classification as a **connective tissue**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Blood:**
 
 
• **Plasma:** This makes up about **55%** of the total **blood volume**. It is a straw-colored liquid consisting of **90-92% water**, **proteins** (like **fibrinogen**, **globulins**, and **albumin**), and **electrolytes**.
 
• **Formed Elements:** These constitute the remaining **45%** and include **Erythrocytes** (**Red Blood Cells**), **Leukocytes** (**White Blood Cells**), and **Thrombocytes** (**Platelets**).
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties:**
 
 
• The **pH** of human blood is slightly **alkaline**, ranging between **7.35 and 7.45**.
 
• In a healthy **adult male**, the average **volume of blood** is approximately **5 to 6 liters**, while in **females**, it is about **4 to 5 liters**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Blood:**
 
 
• **Protection:** **White Blood Cells (WBCs)** provide **immunity** by fighting **pathogens**, and **platelets** facilitate **blood clotting** (**coagulation**) to prevent excessive **blood loss** during injury.
 
• **Regulation:** Blood helps in **thermoregulation** by distributing **heat** throughout the body and maintains **osmotic balance** and **pH levels**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Connective Tissue:**
 
 
• **Loose Connective Tissue:** Examples include **Areolar** and **Adipose** tissues located under the **skin**.
 
• **Dense Connective Tissue:** Includes **Tendons** (connecting **muscle to bone**) and **Ligaments** (connecting **bone to bone**).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about resistivity is correct?

options.text: It depends only on the nature and temperature of the material
It increases with the cross-sectional area
It changes with the shape of the conductor
It decreases when the length increases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It depends only on the nature and temperature of the material**__.

__
 
• **Resistivity**, also known as **specific electrical resistance**, is an intrinsic property of a material that quantifies how strongly it opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• The **resistivity** of a material depends only on the **nature of the material** and its **temperature**. It does not depend on the physical dimensions such as **length** or **cross-sectional area**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **resistance (R)** of a conductor is proportional to its **length (L)** and inversely proportional to its **cross-sectional area (A)**, expressed as **R = ρ (L/A)**, where **ρ (rho)** is the **resistivity**. While resistance changes with area, the **resistivity** constant remains the same for a specific material at a constant temperature. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Since **resistivity** is a material constant, it does not change with the **shape** or **size** of the conductor. Whether the material is shaped into a thin wire or a thick block, its **resistivity** remains identical. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Resistivity** is independent of the **length** of the conductor. If the **length** of a wire is doubled, its **resistance** will double, but its **resistivity** will remain unchanged because it is a characteristic of the substance itself. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• The **SI unit** of **resistivity** is the **Ohm-meter (Ω⋅m)**.
 
• It is represented by the Greek letter **ρ (rho)**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Materials:**
 
 
• **Conductors:** Materials like **Silver** and **Copper** have very low **resistivity**, typically in the range of **10^-8 Ω⋅m**. **Silver** is known to have the lowest **resistivity** (approx **1.59 × 10^-8 Ω⋅m**) at **20°C**.
 
• **Insulators:** Materials like **Glass**, **Rubber**, and **Ebonite** have high **resistivity**, ranging from **10^12 to 10^17 Ω⋅m**.
 
• **Semiconductors:** Materials like **Silicon** and **Germanium** have **resistivity** levels between those of **conductors** and **insulators**.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Effect:**
 
 
• For **metals**, **resistivity** generally increases with an increase in **temperature** because thermal vibrations of atoms interfere with the flow of **electrons**.
 
• For **semiconductors** and **insulators**, **resistivity** usually decreases as **temperature** increases because more **charge carriers** become available for conduction.
 
 
 
• **Alloys:**
 
 
• The **resistivity** of an **alloy** (like **Constantan** or **Manganin**) is generally higher than that of its constituent **metals**.

questions.question: A long straight wire carries a current I , and the magnetic field at a distance r from the conductor is B . If the distance from a straight current-carrying wire is doubled, what will be the magnetic field at that point?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B/2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **magnetic field (B)** produced by a **long straight wire** carrying a **current (I)** at a distance **r** from it is governed by **Ampere’s Circuital Law** or the **Biot-Savart Law**.
 
• The mathematical expression for the **magnetic field** at a point located at a perpendicular distance **r** from an infinitely long straight conductor is given by the formula: **B = (μ₀ * I) / (2 * π * r)**.
 
• In this formula, **μ₀** (mu-naught) represents the **permeability of free space**, **I** is the magnitude of the **electric current**, and **r** is the **radial distance** from the wire.
 
• The relationship between the **magnetic field (B)** and the **distance (r)** is **inversely proportional** (B ∝ 1/r). This implies that if the distance from the wire increases, the strength of the magnetic field decreases proportionally.
 
• According to the question, the initial magnetic field is **B** at distance **r**. When the distance is **doubled**, the new distance becomes **2r**. Substituting this into the formula: **B' = (μ₀ * I) / (2 * π * 2r)**.
 
• By rearranging the equation, we find **B' = 1/2 * [(μ₀ * I) / (2 * π * r)]**. Since the term in the brackets is the original field **B**, the new field is **B/2**. ***Hence, the statement that the magnetic field becomes B/2 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right-Hand Thumb Rule:** This rule is used to determine the **direction** of the **magnetic field lines** around a straight current-carrying conductor. If you hold the wire in your right hand with the **thumb** pointing in the direction of the **current**, the **fingers** will curl in the direction of the **magnetic field lines**.
 
• **Nature of Field Lines:** The **magnetic field lines** around a long straight wire form **concentric circles**. These circles are centered on the wire and exist in a plane **perpendicular** to the direction of the current.
 
• **Permeability of Free Space (μ₀):** This constant defines the strength of the magnetic interaction in a vacuum. Its numerical value is exactly **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A** (Tesla-meter per Ampere).
 
• **Factors Affecting Magnetic Field:**
 
 
• **Current (I):** The field strength is **directly proportional** to the magnitude of the current. Increasing the current increases the magnetic field.
 
• **Distance (r):** The field strength is **inversely proportional** to the distance. Moving further away from the wire results in a weaker magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Unit of Magnetic Field:** The **SI unit** of magnetic field induction is the **Tesla (T)**. Another unit used in the CGS system is the **Gauss (G)**, where **1 Tesla = 10,000 Gauss**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• If the distance were **halved** (r/2) instead of doubled, the **magnetic field** would become **2B** because of the inverse relationship.
 
• For a **finite** length wire, the formula changes to include the angles subtended by the ends of the wire at the point of observation, but for a **long wire** (idealized as infinite), the **1/r** relationship always holds true.
 
• The magnetic field at the **center** of the wire (where r = 0) is theoretically undefined or considered in the context of the wire's thickness, but outside the wire, the **inverse distance** rule is a fundamental principle of **electromagnetism**.

• **Potassium (K):** Helps in maintaining **anion-cation balance** in cells and is involved in **protein synthesis** and the opening and closing of **stomata**.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for Essentiality:** Defined by **Arnon and Stout** in **1939**, it states that the element must be directly involved in plant **metabolism** and its deficiency must be correctable only by supplying that specific element.

• **Critical Concentration:** The limited concentration of an essential element below which plant growth is retarded is termed **critical concentration**.
 
• **Deficiency Symptoms:** When macronutrients are provided in less than the **critical concentration**, plants manifest symptoms like **chlorosis** (yellowing of leaves), **necrosis** (death of tissue), or **stunted growth**.
 
• **Mobility:** Elements like **Nitrogen**, **Potassium**, and **Magnesium** are **mobile** within the plant, meaning deficiency symptoms appear first in **older tissues** as the nutrients are exported to younger leaves. In contrast, **immobile** elements like **Calcium** show symptoms first in **younger tissues**.

⇒ x + y = 45

⇒ x − y = 9

Subtracting the second equation from the first equation:

⇒ 2y = 36

⇒ y = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

• **Fiscal Year:** The **financial year** in India follows a cycle from **April to March**, which is different from the calendar year (January to December).
 
• **Vote on Account:** In an election year, the government usually presents an **Interim Budget** or a **Vote on Account** to meet essential expenditures until a new government is formed. Since **2025-26** is not a general election year, a **full budget** was presented.

questions.question: According to the Sustainable Development Report 2025, what is the percentage of seats held by women in the Indian parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.8%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Report 2025** indicates that the percentage of seats held by women in the **Indian Parliament** stands at **13.8%**. This metric is a vital indicator for monitoring progress toward **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 5**, which focuses on **Gender Equality**.
 
• In the **2024 General Elections**, which formed the **18th Lok Sabha**, a total of **74 women** were elected out of **543 seats**. This resulted in a percentage of approximately **13.6% to 13.8%**, reflecting a slight stagnation in female political representation.
 
• The current figure of **13.8%** shows a marginal decrease compared to the **17th Lok Sabha** (elected in **2019**), where **78 women** were elected, accounting for **14.36%** of the house.
 
• Under the **SDG Indicator 5.5.1**, the proportion of seats held by women in national parliaments is tracked globally to ensure "women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making."
 
• Despite being one of the world's largest democracies, **India's** percentage remains lower than the **global average** of women in national parliaments, which hovers around **26.5%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Bill):**
 
 
• To address the low representation, the **Government of India** passed the **128th Constitutional Amendment Bill** in **September 2023**.
 
• The Act mandates a **33% reservation** for women in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• However, the implementation of this reservation is linked to the completion of the next **census** and the subsequent **delimitation exercise**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Women in Parliament:**
 
 
• In India's **1st Lok Sabha** (formed in **1952**), women held only **4.4%** of the seats.
 
• While the number has grown from **22 women** in **1952** to **74 women** in **2024**, the growth rate has been slow over the last **seven decades**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **SDGs** were adopted by all **United Nations Member States** in **2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty and protect the planet by **2030**.
 
• **SDG 5** specifically targets **gender equality**, including the elimination of all forms of discrimination and violence against women in the public and private spheres.
 
 
 
• **Global and Regional Comparison:**
 
 
• According to reports from the **Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU)**, countries like **Rwanda**, **Cuba**, and **Nicaragua** lead the world with over **50%** women's representation in their national legislatures.
 
• In the **South Asian** region, countries like **Nepal** and **Bangladesh** have historically maintained higher percentages of women in parliament compared to **India** due to various reservation mechanisms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Election Commission of India (ECI):** The **ECI** has noted that while female **voter turnout** has significantly increased (often surpassing male turnout in recent state elections), the number of female **candidates** fielded by political parties remains low.
 
• **Sustainable Development Report:** This report is an annual assessment of progress for all **UN Member States** towards the **SDGs**, published by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**.
 
• **State-wise Performance:** In the **2024 elections**, states like **West Bengal** and **Odisha** showed higher trends of electing women members compared to the national average.
